raw.assessment: The incumbent supplies removable partitions in an assembled, configurable product, but recorded median workshop time exceeds eight minutes and only seven of ten observed customers arranged it unaided. Five missing/incorrect-part reports flag a contents risk without establishing five verified omissions. A limiting observation is D2-O6: repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, so slow completion is not universal. Mixed batches contained the longest orders, but layout complexity and switching remain confounded. D2-O5 likewise does not support width alone as the insertion explanation. These synthetic observations establish neither causes nor pilot success.

openings.claim: Selecting and checking parts across changing orders may contribute to excess time and contents errors; reusable, order-specific staging guides may reduce both.
openings.delta: Stage one complete order against a component checklist before insertion, instead of selecting directly from shared shape bins throughout assembly.
openings.prediction: For matched layout and color, guides reduce selection/checking time and independently audited contents errors; an effect confined to six-compartment insertion would weaken this account.
openings.probe: Have both workers repeat matched orders with and without guides in counterbalanced mixed and grouped sequences. Reuse available samples; time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately and audit contents against orders. Include guide preparation in workshop time accounting.
assumptions: Guides leave product geometry, capacity, colors and compartment counts unchanged.
Preparation and trials fit the delivery schedule and verified initial and recurring cost caps.

openings.claim: Ambiguity in identifying the short partition location may limit unaided arrangement even when all correct parts are present.
openings.delta: Replace the three-layout diagram with a diagram of the ordered layout that identifies the short partition and its orientation.
openings.prediction: With independently verified complete kits, the specific diagram reduces placement questions and increases unaided completion relative to the existing diagram.
openings.probe: Allocate the ten participants across matched first-use sessions with either diagram; record unaided completion, placement errors and questions. Treat this as a directional probe, then assess the stated completeness, time and customer targets in the 60-unit pilot.
assumptions: Diagram production stays within both cost caps and the fixed delivery date.
Supplied parts and removable joints remain unchanged.

raw.assessment: Workshop preassembly is changeable, but its removal has not been validated. Combined timing does not establish insertion as the bottleneck; customer confusion and uncertain fit make simply shipping loose parts unsupported. One interface redesign merits testing.

openings.claim: Replace full workshop assembly with an order-specific flat kit: identify each partition and its matching base-slot position with small marks, and supply a single diagram of the purchased arrangement. A reusable order-specific bench outline verifies the component set before packing. Customers perform the initial reversible insertion.
openings.delta: Delivery would depend on a complete, understandable assembly interface instead of prior workshop insertion. Former obligations must transfer explicitly: correct inventory to the bench outline; selected count and exterior color to an order check; fit and retention to a separate insertion/retention check; spatial guidance to matching marks and the ordered diagram; transport protection to a tested flat-pack restraint. Qualification must retain the 30-by-20-centimeter footprint, assortment capacity, and later dismantling/rearrangement.
openings.prediction: The redesigned kit reduces total workshop time after counting verification and packing, while at least nine of ten initial participants independently produce their ordered arrangement. Persistent short-partition confusion or compensating verification time would challenge the hypothesis.
openings.probe: Use five spare-board samples to test marks, repeated insertion, retention, capacity, and packed handling across all three compartment counts. Use ten further samples with ten participants, recording correct unaided arrangement, missing/incorrect parts, help requests, and completion time. Separately time every workshop activity and cost setup/materials. Treat this as screening only; advance within the fixed delivery schedule only if feasible, then evaluate the 60-unit pilot against at least 59 complete orders, median time at most eight minutes, and at least 90% unaided success.
assumptions: Marks and packing restraint preserve rearrangeability, geometry, capacity, and selected exterior color.
An economical fit/retention check can replace full assembly without losing defect detection.
Setup costs stay within 500, added materials within 0.40 per order, and validation fits the existing delivery date.

openings.claim: Order-specific staging/checklists may reduce selection/checking time and contents errors.
openings.discriminator: Matched-layout/color improvement; insertion-only gains weaken this explanation.
openings.fit: Preserves product; preparation must fit caps/deadline.
openings.probe: Both workers counterbalance guides/no guides and mixed/grouped sequences; time four activities separately, count preparation, independently audit contents.
openings.uncertainty: Complexity and switching confounded; five reports are not five verified omissions.

openings.claim: Ordered-layout diagrams identifying short-partition position/orientation may improve unaided arrangement.
openings.discriminator: Fewer questions and more completions with verified complete kits.
openings.fit: Preserves parts and removable joints; production must fit caps/deadline.
openings.probe: Split ten participants across matched first-use diagram comparisons; record completion, errors, questions.

openings.claim: Marked order-specific flat kits transfer initial insertion to customers; bench outlines verify inventory and ordered diagrams guide placement.
openings.discriminator: Workshop savings including verification/packing plus nine of ten unaided completions.
openings.fit: Uncertain; preserve footprint, capacity, rearrangement, ordered counts/color.
openings.probe: Five samples: all layouts, marks, repeated insertion/retention, capacity, restrained-pack handling. Ten further samples/participants: arrangement, contents, help, time. Check count/color, time all activities, cost setup/materials.
openings.uncertainty: Cheap replacement defect detection, transport protection and usability unproven; width alone unsupported.

post_distill.decision: Probe before adoption; synthetic evidence establishes no cause or success. All options require setup <=500, added materials <=0.40/order, fixed delivery, 30x20 cm footprint and unchanged assortment. Allocate scarce samples/participants deliberately. Qualify any advance in 60-unit pilot: >=59 complete orders, median workshop time <=8 minutes, >=90% unaided arrangement.
